body: High Springs is a small town with a walkable downtown and spring-fed rivers nearby, and many of its homes are worth taking care of. If you need painters in High Springs, FL, Precision Paint Experts is a locally owned contractor based a short drive south in Newberry. We're licensed, bonded, and fully insured in Florida. The people on your ladder are our own crew, not subcontractors.

We've painted in North Central Florida for more than 15 years. The towns across Alachua County share the same humid weather, but the craftsman homes and clapboard siding in High Springs change how we approach the work.

sections.h2: Craftsman trim, clapboard, and downtown storefronts
body: Much of what we paint around Historic Downtown is wood: lap and clapboard siding, deep porch fascia, tapered columns, and multi-part window trim on craftsman-style homes. These houses need patience. Paint gets scraped back to a sound edge, and original profiles are sanded smooth instead of being buried under caulk. Damaged boards get repaired or replaced so they match what's already there. Downtown storefronts need the same care, but on a schedule that keeps the doors open.

Outside the center, Bridlewood and Bailey Estates have newer homes with the usual mix of siding, stucco, and trim. Out along the Poe Springs corridor, there's more acreage, more decks, and more fencing. One town, but three very different kinds of jobs.

sections.h2: Mildew, moisture, and why prep matters
body: High Springs sits in a subtropical climate where mildew and algae grow on anything that stays damp long enough. Shaded clapboard, porch ceilings, and the north side of a house under tree cover are where it shows up first. The color you pick matters less than what happens before it goes on. That means a thorough clean that kills growth at the root, tight caulk joints, and the right primer under the finish.

Wood siding also hides moisture problems. Paint that blisters on one board, or a soft spot below a window, often points to water getting behind the siding. Our article on hidden siding moisture damage explains what to look for. We take moisture readings during the walkthrough so those problems get priced and fixed, not painted over.

sections.h2: From first visit to final walk
body: Walkthroughs are usually scheduled within 48 hours. A crew lead measures, photographs, and probes any suspicious wood, and the itemized estimate usually arrives within one business day. It names every surface included and excluded, the prep, the products, and the number of coats. Nothing is added later without your written approval. Work usually starts one to three weeks after approval.

On older homes, the prep days take the most time: washing, scraping, sanding, mildew treatment, fixing nail pops, replacing rotted boards, re-caulking, and spot-priming. Then come two coats of 100% acrylic on siding and trim, plus a third on porous wood. At the end you walk the job with the crew lead and sign off. Anything that isn't right gets fixed first, and exteriors carry a written warranty of up to 10 years.
From High Springs our crews also cover the city of Alachua to the southeast, Newberry to the south, and across the county line to Fort White and Trenton. When you're ready, request a free estimate.

faqs.a: Yes. Craftsman homes with clapboard siding and original trim make up a lot of our work around Historic Downtown. We scrape to a sound edge, sand the old profiles smooth, and replace rotted boards to match instead of covering them up.

faqs.a: We serve High Springs (32643), including Historic Downtown, Bridlewood, Bailey Estates, and properties along the Poe Springs corridor.

faqs.q: Why does mildew come back on my siding after cleaning?
faqs.a: Pressure alone removes the surface growth but often leaves the roots behind. We soft wash with a cleaning solution that treats the mildew, let the siding dry fully, and then prime and paint.

faqs.q: Are you insured to work in High Springs?
faqs.a: Yes. We're licensed, bonded, and fully insured in Florida, with workers' comp on every crew member. We can provide a certificate of insurance before work begins.
